title: pricing-packaging-scratchpad-lena-2026-03-04
content:
Quick back-of-envelope notes and loose thoughts on token math / unit economics / tier ideas.

---
Context + goals:
- Audience: internal product + finance + go-to-market.
- Goal: get simple per-unit cost model for hosted API (per-token) and reserved capacity (Dedicated) so we can sketch price tiers and expected margins.
- Constraints: keep things simple for initial sketch; capture major cost drivers (GPU cycles, memory, IO, infra, support).

Assumptions (placeholder numbers — refine with infra team):
- Model footprints: small gen model (7B) vs mid (13-20B) vs large (70B+). For hosted pricing we will standardize into 3 buckets: small / medium / large.
- Tokens per request: typical chat turn = 80 tokens output + 120 tokens context (prompt + system + history) => 200 tokens/turn.
- Average tokens per session (multi-turn): 4 turns => 800 tokens/session.
- Requests per second and batching: assume effective batching reduces compute cost by ~1.2x vs no batching for hosted. Dedicated can get ~1.6x depending on workload.

Compute cost basis (very rough):
- GPU-hour effective cost (amortized incl infra, ops, S3, networking, etc): $2.50/hr for shared-hosted infra (highly optimized, spot + pooling). Dedicated amortized infra cost higher once you include reserved pricing/SLAs: $7.00/hr per GPU (account for Opex + reserved capacity).
- Effective throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU (varies by model):
  * small: 12k tokens/sec/GPU
  * medium: 6k tokens/sec/GPU
  * large: 1.5k tokens/sec/GPU
- Therefore raw compute cost per 1k tokens (compute only):
  * small: (1k tokens) / (12k tok/sec) = 0.0833 sec -> cost = 2.5 * (0.0833/3600) = $0.0000576 ~ 0.000058 USD per 1k tokens
  * medium: 1k/6k = 0.1667 sec -> cost = 2.5 * (0.1667/3600) = $0.000116 ~ 0.00012 USD per 1k tokens
  * large: 1k/1.5k = 0.6667 sec -> cost = 2.5 * (0.6667/3600) = $0.000463 ~ 0.00046 USD per 1k tokens
- For Dedicated (use $7/hr GPU): multiply numbers by 7/2.5 = 2.8x -> per-1k tokens compute cost roughly 0.00016 / 0.00034 / 0.0013 for small/med/large respectively.

Other cost buckets (per-1k-token equivalents estimate):
- Network egress & storage: $0.00005 per 1k tokens (includes object storage reads for model shards, small but non-zero).
- KV cache / redis amortized: $0.00002 per 1k tokens (depends heavily on hit rate; if we have prefix caching, can drop effective token compute).
- Orchestration + routing + api infra (k8s, control plane, endpoints): $0.00003 per 1k tokens.
- Support & SRE + monitoring + margin for variability: $0.0001 per 1k tokens (blunt overhead).
- Total hosted variable cost per 1k tokens (approx):
  * small: 0.000058 + 0.00005 + 0.00002 + 0.00003 + 0.0001 = 0.000258 USD per 1k tokens (~0.00026)
  * medium: 0.00012 + overheads = ~0.00032 USD per 1k tokens
  * large: 0.00046 + overheads = ~0.00064 USD per 1k tokens

Pricing sketch (hosted API): markup target ~4–6x variable cost for self‑serve customers (to cover R&D, churn, discounts, multi-tenant risk). For enterprise / committed customers we can offer lower unit prices.
- Suggested list prices (per 1k tokens):
  * small: $0.0012 per 1k tokens (approx 4.6x hosted variable cost)
  * medium: $0.0020 per 1k tokens (approx 6x variable cost)
  * large: $0.0050 per 1k tokens (approx 7.8x variable cost) -> note: large models have higher fixed Opex and support SLA expectations; price sensitivity lower.

Free tier / credits:
- Free tier: 100k tokens/month (to encourage experimentation). Cost to us: 100k * variable small cost (~0.00026) = $0.026 per free user per month — seems fine for viral acquisition.

Developer examples (customer-visible pricing examples):
- Small model: 800 tokens/session -> ~0.8 * (0.0012/1k) = $0.00000096 per session? Wait need consistent units. Better: 800 tokens = 0.8 * 1k => cost = 0.8 * $0.0012 = $0.00096 per session.
  * So 1M sessions (~800M tokens) costs $960.
- Medium model: 800 tokens -> 0.8 * $0.0020 = $0.0016 per session. 1M sessions -> $1,600.
- Large model: 800 tokens -> 0.8 * $0.0050 = $0.004 per session. 1M sessions -> $4,000.

Embeddings pricing (different unit):
- Embedding cost tied to vectorization compute + IO. Typical approach: price per 1k tokens or per embedding (if fixed input sizes).
- Quick sketch: variable cost per 1k tokens for embeddings ~ $0.0008 (higher because compute tends to be heavier relative to throughput).
- List price: $0.005 per 1k tokens for embeddings (or $0.0003 per embedding for small fixed-length inputs) — needs refinement.

Reserved / Dedicated pricing sketch (for teams with steady usage):
- Two billing components: reserved infra fee (monthly) + discounted per-token/throughput pricing for excess/burst.
- Example small cluster (single 8-GPU K80-equivalent? but we use modern GPUs so think 8xA10/80GB equivalents):
  * Dedicated small: 4 GPUs reserved -> cost to Redwood (amortized) say $X = 4 * $7/hr * 24 * 30 = $20160/month (base infra). Add operator+support overhead -> $25k/month.
  * Offer customers a committed price of $12k/month for that pool with throughput SLA; allow shared tenancy inside customer. That implies we price reserved capacity at a significant discount vs per-token hosted for heavy customers.
- Alternatively price Dedicated by committed QPS or tokens/hour: e.g., $YY per 1k tokens processed under dedicated SLA (lower than hosted list by 30–60%).

Simpler packaging ideas (tier names + rough pricing):
- Hobby / Dev (self-serve): Free up to 100k tokens/mo, then pay-as-you-go: small $0.0012 /1k, embeddings $0.005/1k.
- Startup: $99/mo includes 5M tokens included (small), overage at $0.0009/1k. Limited support, email only.
- Growth: $499/mo includes 30M tokens, overage at $0.0007/1k. Phone support + 30-day retention.
- Scale: $2,500/mo includes 200M tokens, overage at $0.0005/1k. Priority support, per-route dashboards.
- Dedicated (Reserved): starts $12k/mo (4-GPU pool) => best for steady high throughput. Custom SLAs and private networking.
- Private / On-prem: license + install + support (custom pricing).

Examples to sanity-check margins:
- A Growth customer (499/mo) using full included 30M tokens: cost to us (30M * 0.00026) = $7.8 -> clearly huge margin on small model usage. But many tokens will be med/large and overhead/marketing/support must be covered; top-line seems plausible for PLG motion.

Open questions / follow-ups to tighten model:
1) Get real GPU-hour effective cost from infra finance (spot vs reserved blended). Also different for region (us-west vs eu-west).
2) Get accurate throughput numbers per GPU for our actual models (profile 7B/13B/70B using production runtime with batching & KV cache).
3) Measure avg tokens/session across self-serve signups (we have some analytics but need distribution).
4) Calculate KV cache hit-rate sensitivity to token cost — cache could materially lower effective token compute in chat flows.
5) Embeddings: measure CPU/GPU mix and cost of vector DB ops (we currently offload to customer-managed DBs often).
6) Sales/Legal input on committed pricing structure, minimum commitment terms, and credits for overage.

Loose thoughts / heuristics:
- Use simple round numbers for public pricing to avoid confusing customers (e.g., $0.0012 -> round to $0.0015 or $0.001?). But keep internal model accurate.
- Consider per-request SLO tiers (best-effort vs low-latency): price low-latency higher (because it constrains batching and increases per-token cost).
- Offer model family labels instead of raw model sizes (e.g., Redwood-S, Redwood-M, Redwood-L) so we can migrate underlying model without changing price names.
- Offer embedding-batch discounts (per-embedding or per-1k tokens bundle).
- For Dedicated, consider dual pricing: base reserved monthly + very cheap overage per token (fits customers who want steady baseline).
- Consider usage commitments with annual discounts for large customers.

Notes to self:
- Need to run 3 microbenchmarks with serving runtime: 7B (fp16), 13B (q4_k_maybe), 70B (int8-ish) – measure tokens/sec and 95thpct latency for 1,2,4,8 concurrent streams.
- Ask infra for per-region cost breakdown (GPUs, networking, storage).
- Draft a small spreadsheet that maps tokens/sec -> $/1k tokens including overhead buckets; produce estimator for sales to run quick quotes.

Bottom line (for now):
- Per-1k token variable costs are tiny (<< a penny). We should price to capture serious margin for PLG while being competitive in market. Dedicated/Private pricing should move to a capacity/commitment model where unit prices drop.

TODO:
- [ ] Confirm GPU-hour blended cost with finance (assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Run throughput microbenchmarks on 3 target models (assigned: Eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] Build a one-page pricing spreadsheet/estimate tool for Sales

End of scratchpad.
